intent.raw_query: Swiss Alps ski holiday family, $7000, 7 days, February

experiences.name: Zermatt Ski Resort Full-Day Pass
experiences.description: Ski the world-famous slopes of Zermatt with stunning views of the Matterhorn. With over 360km of marked runs, this resort caters to all skill levels. Book slopes near the village base to maximize time after a late Day 1 arrival, starting fresh on Day 2. Stay in Zermatt village to walk to lifts each morning.

experiences.name: Jungfrau Region Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking
experiences.description: Explore the breathtaking Jungfrau region on guided snowshoe trails through pristine alpine landscapes. Trails depart directly from Grindelwald village center, making it ideal for those staying locally. A perfect mid-week activity after ski days, requiring no special equipment rental beyond snowshoes included in the tour.

experiences.name: St. Moritz Ice Skating & Bobsled Experience
experiences.description: Skate on the legendary frozen Lake St. Moritz and optionally ride the historic Olympia Bob Run, one of the world's oldest natural ice bobsled tracks. Both attractions are within walking distance of St. Moritz village center, eliminating transfer time. Best enjoyed mid-afternoon when ice conditions are optimal.

experiences.name: Swiss Alpine Cheese & Fondue Cultural Evening
experiences.description: Join a traditional Swiss fondue and raclette dinner experience in a historic mountain chalet in Verbier village. Learn about centuries-old Alpine cheese-making culture while warming up after a day on the slopes. Restaurants are clustered in the village center, perfect for guests staying in Verbier accommodations.

experiences.name: Glacier 3000 Cable Car & Snow Bus Adventure
experiences.description: Ride the iconic cable car to Glacier 3000 above Les Diablerets for panoramic views across four countries. Experience the Snow Bus ride across the glacier plateau and visit the Peak Walk suspension bridge connecting two mountain peaks. The base station is a short walk from Les Diablerets village, ideal for a full afternoon excursion on a rest day from skiing.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich or Milan Malpensa airport, take a regional train or bus toward Poschiavo via the Bernina Express route. Check in to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Settle in, unpack, and get a good night's rest to prepare for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick and affordable bite at the airport or train station (sandwiches, pretzels, or a kebab wrap for ~CHF 8-12). Alternatively, pick up snacks at a Migros or Coop convenience store en route.

day_by_day.notes: The Bernina Express route from Chur to Tirano passes through Poschiavo — a scenic and budget-friendly way to arrive. Book train tickets in advance via SBB.ch for the best fares. The B&B may have a late check-in arrangement; confirm with the host beforehand. Keep CHF cash on hand as smaller establishments in Poschiavo may not accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: After a hearty B&B breakfast, take a short walk to explore the charming village of Poschiavo. Stroll through the historic Piazza Comunale, admire the Spanish-style architecture unique to this Graubünden valley, and visit the local market if open. The crisp mountain air and snow-dusted rooftops make for a beautiful introduction to the Swiss Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby Lago di Poschiavo (Lake Poschiavo), which may be partially frozen in February — a stunning winter spectacle. Walk along the lakeside path (~3 km loop) and take in panoramic views of the surrounding snow-capped peaks. This is a free activity and perfect for photography and acclimatization.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the village center and explore the local shops. Visit the Coop or local grocery store to stock up on budget-friendly snacks, fruit, and drinks for the week. Relax at the B&B and plan the upcoming ski days.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — enjoy local bread, cheese, cold cuts, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch with items from the local Coop supermarket — bread, cheese, salami, and fruit for ~CHF 8-10.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Albrici in Poschiavo — a local favorite offering traditional Graubünden cuisine. Try the pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta) or polenta dishes for ~CHF 18-25. Budget-friendly by Swiss standards.

day_by_day.notes: Poschiavo sits at about 1,014 m elevation. Take it easy today to acclimatize before hitting the slopes. The lake walk is flat and accessible. Wear warm, waterproof layers as February temperatures can drop to -5°C to -10°C at night.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Bernina Express train (or PostBus) from Poschiavo up to Pontresina or St. Moritz — both accessible within 30-45 minutes. Head to the Diavolezza ski area, one of the most spectacular glacier ski resorts in the Alps. Purchase a day ski pass (look for early-bird or online discounts; ~CHF 65-75 for adults). Rent ski equipment at the base if needed (~CHF 35-45/day for budget rental packages). Hit the slopes by mid-morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing at Diavolezza. The resort offers runs for all levels, with breathtaking views of the Morteratsch Glacier and Piz Palü. Try the famous Diavolezza glacier run — a 10 km off-piste descent (guided or with experience). Take a break at the mountain restaurant for a warm drink and enjoy the alpine panorama.
day_by_day.evening: Return by train to Poschiavo. Soak tired muscles with a warm shower. Spend a relaxed evening at the B&B or take a short evening stroll through the illuminated village streets.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B.
meals.lunch: Pack a homemade sandwich and thermos of hot tea/coffee from the B&B to save money on mountain restaurant prices. Supplement with a CHF 4-5 hot chocolate at the mountain hut.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple pasta or soup using groceries from Coop (~CHF 5-8 per person) if the B&B has a guest kitchen, or try Pizzeria da Rino in Poschiavo for a pizza from ~CHF 16-20.

day_by_day.notes: Book ski passes online in advance at diavolezza.ch for potential discounts. The Bernina Pass road may be closed in winter — use the train. Bring sunscreen as UV rays are intense at altitude even in winter. Helmet rental is recommended (~CHF 8/day extra).

day_by_day.morning: Take the PostBus or train toward Livigno (just across the Italian border, ~45 min from Poschiavo via Trepalle). Livigno is a duty-free ski resort offering significantly cheaper ski passes, equipment rentals, and food compared to Swiss resorts. Purchase a day ski pass (~€35-45) and rent equipment if needed (~€20-30). Start skiing the wide, sunny slopes of Livigno.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Livigno's extensive ski area — 115 km of pistes suitable for all levels. The resort is known for its long, wide runs and excellent snow conditions in February. Take advantage of the duty-free status to grab affordable snacks and drinks at the base village shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by early evening. Visit a local Poschiavo café or bar for an aperitivo — a glass of local wine or Spritz for ~CHF 5-8. Enjoy a quiet evening at the B&B.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B.
meals.lunch: Eat at a mountain restaurant in Livigno — prices are much lower than Switzerland. A pasta dish or pizza costs ~€10-14. Great value for a ski lunch.
meals.dinner: Trattoria-style dinner in Livigno before heading back (~€12-18 for pasta and a drink), or cook at the B&B using groceries.

day_by_day.notes: Bring your passport as you are crossing into Italy. Livigno is a duty-free zone — stock up on affordable chocolate, wine, and snacks. Check PostBus schedules carefully as services may be limited in winter. The border crossing at Forcola di Livigno is typically open in winter but verify conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day from skiing. After breakfast, take the Bernina Express train northward to Pontresina (~30 min, ~CHF 10-12 one way with Swiss Travel Pass or regional ticket). Explore this charming alpine village on foot. Visit the Pontresina Museum or the Romanesque murals in the Santa Maria Chapel (free or minimal entry fee).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or snowshoe the Roseg Valley trail from Pontresina — a flat, scenic 8 km round-trip trail through a pristine winter landscape toward the Roseg Glacier. Snowshoe rentals are available in Pontresina (~CHF 15-20/day). This is one of the most beautiful free winter walks in the Engadin valley.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by train. Treat yourself to a fondue or raclette dinner — the quintessential Swiss Alps experience. Look for a local restaurant offering a set fondue menu for ~CHF 25-30 per person.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from B&B or grab a bratwurst and bread from a Pontresina bakery/butcher for ~CHF 8-10.
meals.dinner: Fondue dinner at a local Poschiavo restaurant or a Pontresina mountain restaurant. Ristorante Albrici or Hotel Albrici in Poschiavo may offer seasonal fondue. Budget ~CHF 25-30 per person including a drink.

day_by_day.notes: The Roseg Valley walk is free and one of the most rewarding winter experiences in the region. Wear waterproof boots with good grip. The trail is generally well-packed but can be icy — microspikes or snowshoes are recommended. Check train schedules at sbb.ch.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the slopes for a final ski day. This time, head to Corvatsch or Corviglia ski areas near St. Moritz (~45 min by train from Poschiavo). These are world-class ski areas with stunning Engadin views. Purchase a half-day ski pass to save money (~CHF 45-55 for afternoon or morning half-day). Focus on intermediate and advanced runs with panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing until early afternoon. Explore the free cross-country ski trails (Langlauf) around St. Moritz Lake if you want a change of pace — the Engadin valley has over 200 km of groomed cross-country trails, some of which are free to use.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo. Spend the evening packing and preparing for departure. Take a final evening walk through Poschiavo's historic center and enjoy a farewell drink at a local bar.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B.
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant at Corvatsch or Corviglia — budget for a soup and bread (~CHF 12-16) or bring a packed lunch.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a local Poschiavo restaurant. Try the local specialty of Pizzoccheri della Valchiavenna or a hearty Graubünden barley soup (Bündner Gerstensuppe) for ~CHF 18-24.

day_by_day.notes: St. Moritz can be expensive — avoid the luxury hotels and restaurants in the village center. Stick to mountain huts and packed lunches. The cross-country trails around the lake are a fantastic free activity. Saturday may be busier on the slopes — arrive early to beat the crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely breakfast at the B&B. Check out and store luggage if needed. Take a short final walk around Poschiavo to soak in the mountain atmosphere. Visit the local Sunday market if available, or browse the small artisan shops for affordable Swiss souvenirs (local honey, dried meats, or Graubünden wine).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Poschiavo by Bernina Express train toward Chur, Zurich, or Milan depending on your return flight. The Bernina Express itself is a UNESCO World Heritage railway journey — a spectacular final memory of the Swiss Alps. Enjoy the dramatic viaducts, glaciers, and mountain scenery from the comfort of the train.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your departure airport. Allow ample time for check-in and security. Reflect on an incredible week of skiing, mountain scenery, and Swiss alpine culture.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B — enjoy the final home-cooked Swiss breakfast.
meals.lunch: Pack remaining groceries for a train picnic, or grab a Migros or Coop takeaway at the train station (~CHF 8-12).
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal. Budget for ~CHF 15-20 at airport food courts if needed.

day_by_day.notes: The Bernina Express panoramic car upgrade costs ~CHF 15-20 extra but is highly recommended for the final journey — a stunning way to end the trip. Book in advance at rhb.ch. Confirm your return flight details and allow at least 3 hours from Poschiavo to Zurich Airport or 2.5 hours to Milan Malpensa. Keep CHF and EUR for last-minute purchases.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Transfer from airport to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Check in, settle into your room, and get a good night's rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama around 23:30–00:00 depending on transfer. Grab a light snack if available at the B&B or from any provisions you carry. Rest and prepare for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport meal
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight or airport meal
meals.dinner: Light snack upon arrival — pick up something at the airport (e.g., a sandwich or pastry from a kiosk) before the transfer to Poschiavo

day_by_day.notes: Poschiavo is a scenic village in the Graubünden canton near the Italian border. Transfer from Zurich or Milan Malpensa airport takes approximately 2.5–3 hours by car or train. Pre-arrange a taxi or rental car. The Bernina Express train is not available at this late hour, so a private transfer is recommended. Pack warm layers — temperatures in Poschiavo in February average -2°C to 4°C.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the B&B to recover from travel. After breakfast, take a gentle orientation walk through the charming historic village of Poschiavo — explore the Piazza Comunale, the Spanish Quarter (La Rösa), and the Church of San Vittore. Get acquainted with the stunning alpine surroundings and breathe in the crisp mountain air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the local Poschiavo Valley ski area or the nearby Livigno ski resort (approx. 30 minutes by car across the Italian border). Livigno offers excellent beginner-to-intermediate slopes and is a great warm-up day on the snow. Rent ski equipment locally if needed. Enjoy a few hours of skiing or snowboarding on well-groomed pistes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by late afternoon. Freshen up at the B&B, then head into the village for dinner at a local restaurant. Explore the cozy trattorias and Swiss-Italian fusion eateries that reflect Poschiavo's unique cultural blend.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — enjoy local bread, cheese, cold cuts, yogurt, and coffee included with your stay
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant lunch on the slopes at Livigno — try a hearty plate of pasta or a local mountain dish (budget CHF 20–35)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ristorante Suisse or Osteria Serta in Poschiavo — enjoy Swiss-Italian cuisine such as pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta with cheese and vegetables), polenta, or local cured meats (budget CHF 30–50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Livigno is technically in Italy but is a duty-free zone — fuel and alcohol are cheaper there. Bring your passport for the border crossing. Ski rental in Livigno is generally more affordable than in major Swiss resorts. Confirm B&B breakfast times the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast at the B&B, then depart for St. Moritz (approximately 45 minutes by car or 1 hour via the scenic Bernina Express train). Upon arrival, head to the legendary frozen Lake St. Moritz for the St. Moritz Ice Skating & Bobsled Experience. Lace up your skates and glide across one of the world's most iconic frozen lakes with a stunning alpine backdrop.
day_by_day.afternoon: After ice skating, take the thrilling optional ride on the historic Olympia Bob Run — one of the oldest natural ice bobsled tracks in the world, dating back to 1904. This adrenaline-pumping experience is a bucket-list winter activity. Afterward, stroll through the glamorous St. Moritz village, window-shop along Via Serlas, and soak in the upscale alpine atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in St. Moritz before returning to Poschiavo. Opt for a mid-range restaurant that captures the St. Moritz charm without the ultra-luxury price tag. Return to the B&B by 21:00–22:00.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Hauser in St. Moritz — a beloved local institution famous for its homemade cakes, soups, and sandwiches (budget CHF 25–40)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Engiadina in St. Moritz — a cozy, authentic spot serving traditional Engadine dishes like Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup) and Capuns (chard-wrapped dumplings) at reasonable prices (budget CHF 35–55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Bernina Express from Poschiavo to St. Moritz is a UNESCO World Heritage railway journey — highly recommended for the scenic experience (approx. CHF 20–30 one way). Book the Olympia Bob Run experience in advance as slots fill up quickly. The bobsled experience costs approximately CHF 150–200 per person. Ice skating rental is available on-site at the lake.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, embark on a full-day trip to Zermatt for the Zermatt Ski Resort Full-Day Pass experience. Depart early (by 07:00) as the journey from Poschiavo to Zermatt takes approximately 3–3.5 hours by car and train (drive to Visp or Täsch, then take the Zermatt shuttle train — private cars are not allowed in Zermatt). Purchase your full-day ski pass and hit the world-famous slopes with over 360km of marked runs and breathtaking views of the iconic Matterhorn.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing through Zermatt's legendary terrain. Take the Klein Matterhorn cable car to Europe's highest ski area at 3,883m for panoramic views across four countries. Intermediate skiers will love the Gornergrat and Rothorn areas, while advanced skiers can tackle the challenging off-piste routes. Take a mid-afternoon break at a mountain restaurant to refuel.
day_by_day.evening: Ski until late afternoon, then begin the return journey to Poschiavo. Grab a quick dinner in Visp or Brig on the way back, or pick up provisions for a simple meal at the B&B. Arrive back in Poschiavo by 21:00–22:00.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at B&B — pack an energy bar or snack for the journey
meals.lunch: Lunch at Findlerhof Restaurant on the Zermatt slopes — a charming mountain hut with stunning Matterhorn views, serving rösti, soups, and hot drinks (budget CHF 30–45)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Walliserkanne in Zermatt village before departure (budget CHF 35–55) OR a quick stop at a Migros or Coop supermarket in Visp for a budget-friendly takeaway meal on the road

day_by_day.notes: This is the longest travel day of the trip — plan carefully. Täsch parking costs approximately CHF 15/day. The Zermatt shuttle train from Täsch costs CHF 10 return. A full-day ski pass in Zermatt costs approximately CHF 90–110 per person. Ski rental is available in Zermatt but book in advance online for discounts. Dress in warm, waterproof layers — altitude at the top stations can be -15°C or colder. Consider an early departure to maximize ski time.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the big Zermatt day. Enjoy a relaxed breakfast at the B&B. Then join the Jungfrau Region Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking experience — depart mid-morning toward the Jungfrau region (approximately 2.5 hours from Poschiavo). The guided snowshoe tour takes you through pristine alpine landscapes, frozen forests, and breathtaking mountain scenery around Grindelwald or Wengen.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the guided snowshoe tour through the afternoon. The Jungfrau region offers spectacular views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau peaks. The guide will share insights about alpine ecology, local traditions, and mountain safety. This is a wonderful contrast to the high-speed skiing days — a peaceful, immersive way to experience the Swiss Alps.
day_by_day.evening: After the tour, enjoy dinner in the Jungfrau region (Grindelwald or Interlaken) before the return drive to Poschiavo. Alternatively, if returning earlier, dine in Poschiavo at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at B&B Berninahaus Poschiavo Panorama
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by the snowshoe tour guide OR stop at a mountain hut along the trail — try traditional Älplermagronen (alpine macaroni with cheese, potatoes, and applesauce) (budget CHF 20–35)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Onkel Tom's Hütte in Grindelwald — a cozy, rustic spot with excellent Swiss classics and a warm atmosphere (budget CHF 35–50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Jungfrau Region Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking experience in advance. Snowshoe rentals are typically included or available for CHF 10–15. Wear waterproof hiking boots and warm, breathable layers. The tour is suitable for all fitness levels — no prior snowshoeing experience required. The return drive from Grindelwald to Poschiavo is approximately 2.5 hours — plan to depart by 18:00 to arrive at a reasonable hour.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, depart for the Glacier 3000 Cable Car & Snow Bus Adventure near Les Diablerets (approximately 3 hours from Poschiavo). Ride the iconic cable car from Col du Pillon up to Glacier 3000 at 3,000m elevation. Marvel at panoramic views spanning four countries — Switzerland, France, Italy, and Germany. Walk across the thrilling Peak Walk suspension bridge connecting two mountain peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board the unique Snow Bus — a specially designed vehicle that drives across the glacier — for an unforgettable adventure on the ice. Enjoy optional activities at the summit including snow tubing, ski runs, and the glacier walk. Take time to visit the Botta Hut restaurant at the summit for a warm drink and to soak in the extraordinary views. Descend by cable car in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Join the Swiss Alpine Cheese & Fondue Cultural Evening — a traditional Swiss fondue and raclette dinner experience in a historic mountain chalet in the Verbier/Les Diablerets area. This immersive cultural evening includes local cheeses, wines, and stories about Swiss alpine traditions. A perfect way to celebrate the penultimate evening of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurant Botta 3000 at the Glacier 3000 summit — enjoy panoramic views while dining on Swiss mountain cuisine (budget CHF 30–50)
meals.dinner: Swiss Alpine Cheese & Fondue Cultural Evening — traditional fondue, raclette, local wines, and Swiss hospitality in a historic mountain chalet (budget CHF 55–80 per person including drinks)

day_by_day.notes: The Glacier 3000 cable car ticket costs approximately CHF 45–55 per person return. The Snow Bus experience is included with the cable car ticket. Book the Fondue Cultural Evening in advance as it is a popular experience. After dinner, the drive back to Poschiavo is approximately 3 hours — consider booking a nearby accommodation in the Les Diablerets or Gstaad area for this night to avoid a very late return, or depart the fondue evening by 21:00 for a midnight arrival in Poschiavo.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Take a slow morning walk through Poschiavo village one last time — visit the local Sunday market if available, pick up Swiss souvenirs such as local cheeses, chocolates, Bündner Nusstorte (walnut tart), or Graubünden wines. Pack your bags and check out of the B&B.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight, spend the early afternoon on a final scenic drive along the Bernina Pass road — one of Switzerland's most spectacular mountain roads — stopping at viewpoints to photograph the glaciers, frozen lakes, and alpine peaks. Alternatively, enjoy a final short ski session at Livigno (30 minutes away) if time permits before heading to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to your departure airport (Zurich approximately 3 hours, Milan Malpensa approximately 2.5 hours). Allow ample time for check-in and security. Reflect on an incredible week of skiing, winter adventures, and Swiss alpine culture.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — savor the local cheeses and breads one last time
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Roseg in Pontresina (20 minutes from Poschiavo) — a charming café with homemade soups, sandwiches, and Swiss pastries (budget CHF 20–35) OR grab provisions from the local Poschiavo Coop supermarket for a picnic at a scenic viewpoint
meals.dinner: Airport dinner at departure terminal OR an early dinner in Lugano or Bellinzona if routing through Ticino (try a local risotto or polenta dish at a trattoria, budget CHF 30–45)

day_by_day.notes: Check B&B checkout time (typically 10:00–11:00). Confirm your return flight details and calculate transfer time carefully — Swiss roads in February can be affected by snow or ice, so add 30–45 minutes buffer to your travel time. Purchase any last-minute Swiss souvenirs in Poschiavo or at the airport. The Bernina Pass road (Route 29) may be closed in severe winter conditions — check road conditions at viasuisse.ch before driving. Consider purchasing Swiss chocolate, Graubünden wine, or a Bündner Nusstorte as gifts.

meals.lunch: Not applicable — in transit
meals.dinner: Light in-room dining or welcome snack arranged by the property upon arrival. Consider pre-arranging a charcuterie board and local Swiss wine with the hotel in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private luxury transfer (e.g., via Swiss Limousine Service or Blacklane) from Zurich or Milan Malpensa airport depending on your routing. The drive to Poschiavo is scenic but can take 2–3 hours. Confirm late check-in with the property. Pack layers — Poschiavo sits at approximately 1,014m elevation and February nights are cold.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late breakfast at the B&B to recover from travel. Explore the charming historic village of Poschiavo on foot — stroll through the Piazza Comunale, admire the Spanish-style architecture of the historic quarter, and visit the local artisan shops. This gentle orientation walk sets the tone for the alpine adventure ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or arrange a private transfer along the scenic Bernina Pass road (one of Switzerland's most spectacular mountain routes) for a self-guided winter exploration. Stop at Lago Bianco — a stunning frozen alpine lake at 2,234m — for photography and a crisp alpine walk. The surrounding snow-covered peaks offer a dramatic introduction to the Swiss Alps.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo for a refined dinner at Ristorante Suisse or a top-rated local establishment in the village. Enjoy regional Graubünden cuisine featuring hearty alpine dishes such as Pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta), venison ragù, and local Poschiavo wines.

meals.breakfast: Full Swiss breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — expect fresh bread, local cheeses, cold cuts, jams, and coffee with panoramic mountain views.
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet picnic arranged by the hotel, or stop at a mountain café along the Bernina Pass road for hot soup, Rösti, and mulled wine.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Suisse, Poschiavo — a beloved local institution serving authentic Graubünden cuisine. Reserve a table by the fireplace for a cozy, premium alpine dining experience. Budget CHF 80–130 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Bernina Pass road (Route 29) may have winter driving restrictions — confirm road conditions and consider hiring a local driver or 4WD rental. The Bernina Express train also runs through this corridor and offers a spectacular alternative for the afternoon excursion. Dress in full winter layers for the Lago Bianco stop.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to St. Moritz — approximately 45 minutes from Poschiavo via the Bernina Pass or by the iconic Bernina Express train. Begin the morning with the St. Moritz Ice Skating & Bobsled Experience: skate on the legendary frozen Lake St. Moritz, one of the world's most glamorous winter venues. The natural ice rink is maintained to perfection and surrounded by five-star hotels and mountain panoramas.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, take on the historic Olympia Bob Run — one of the oldest and most thrilling bobsled tracks in the world, dating to 1904. Experience the adrenaline of reaching speeds up to 130 km/h on a natural ice track as a passenger alongside a professional pilot. This is a bucket-list winter sports experience exclusive to St. Moritz.
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in a world-class dinner in St. Moritz before returning to Poschiavo. St. Moritz offers some of Switzerland's finest dining — choose from Michelin-starred establishments for an unforgettable culinary evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at B&B before departure — fuel up with a hearty Swiss spread before the day's adventures.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mathis Food Affairs or Roo Bar at Hotel Hauser in St. Moritz — chic alpine dining with stunning lake views. Expect premium burgers, truffle pasta, and craft cocktails. Budget CHF 60–100 per person.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Acla da Fans at Kulm Hotel St. Moritz or Ecco St. Moritz (Michelin-starred) — an exceptional fine dining experience featuring modern Alpine cuisine with impeccable wine pairings. Budget CHF 180–300 per person. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Olympia Bob Run experience in advance at olympia-bobrun.ch — passenger rides are available on select days and fill up quickly. The Bernina Express train between Poschiavo and St. Moritz is a UNESCO World Heritage railway journey and highly recommended over driving for the scenic experience. Purchase first-class tickets. Dress in smart-casual attire for evening dining in St. Moritz.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure for a full-day excursion to Zermatt — Switzerland's most iconic ski destination. Travel via private luxury transfer or train connections (approximately 3–4 hours from Poschiavo). Upon arrival in the car-free village of Zermatt, check your gear and head directly to the slopes for the Zermatt Ski Resort Full-Day Pass. With over 360km of marked runs and the majestic Matterhorn as your backdrop, the morning session offers the best snow conditions and lighter crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing across Zermatt's three interconnected ski areas — Rothorn, Stockhorn, and Klein Matterhorn (the highest ski area in the Alps at 3,883m). Take the Matterhorn Glacier Paradise cable car for breathtaking 360-degree views across four countries. Intermediate and advanced skiers will revel in the variety of terrain, from groomed pistes to off-piste powder fields.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski in Zermatt — the village transforms into a lively yet sophisticated scene after 4pm. Visit the legendary Hennu Stall or Papperla Pub for a celebratory Glühwein before a gourmet dinner. Given the distance, consider an overnight stay in Zermatt (upgrade option) or return to Poschiavo via private transfer.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at B&B before departure — or grab a premium coffee and pastry at a Zermatt café upon arrival.
meals.lunch: On-mountain lunch at Chez Vrony — one of Switzerland's most celebrated mountain restaurants, perched at 2,000m with direct Matterhorn views. Famous for their Valais beef, homemade pasta, and local wines. Reserve ahead. Budget CHF 80–120 per person.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Zum See in Zermatt — a rustic yet refined mountain restaurant accessible by ski or foot, serving exceptional Valais cuisine in a fairy-tale setting. Alternatively, dine at Restaurant Capri at The Omnia hotel for Italian-Alpine fusion with panoramic views. Budget CHF 120–200 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt is car-free — all transfers within the village use electric taxis or horse-drawn carriages. Rent high-performance ski equipment in advance through Zermatt's premium rental shops (e.g., Slalom Sport or Bayard Sport) or arrange through a concierge service. A private ski guide (CHF 500–700/day) is highly recommended to maximize your time on the best runs. Consider booking one night in Zermatt at The Omnia or Mont Cervin Palace to avoid the long return journey — this is a worthy luxury upgrade.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the Poschiavo base (if you stayed overnight in Zermatt, depart after a leisurely breakfast). Once back in the Graubünden region, embark on the Glacier 3000 Cable Car & Snow Bus Adventure — a day trip to Les Diablerets above Gstaad (approximately 3 hours from Poschiavo). Ride the iconic Peak Walk by Tissot suspension bridge — the world's first suspension bridge connecting two mountain peaks — for jaw-dropping panoramic views across the Bernese, Vaud, and Valais Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Experience the Snow Bus — a thrilling ride across the glacier plateau on a specially designed snow vehicle. Explore the glacier on foot, try snow tubing, or take a guided glacier walk. The area also offers excellent off-piste skiing and snowboarding for adventurous guests. The views across four countries (Switzerland, France, Italy, Germany) on a clear day are absolutely extraordinary.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo for a relaxed evening. Treat yourself to a private in-room spa experience or arrange a massage through the hotel. Enjoy a quiet, intimate dinner in the village.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Zermatt hotel (if overnight) or at B&B Berninapass upon return — fresh alpine dairy, local honey, and artisan breads.
meals.lunch: Restaurant Botta 3000 at Glacier 3000 — a stunning glass-and-steel mountain restaurant designed by architect Mario Botta, offering panoramic glacier views and refined Swiss-Mediterranean cuisine. Budget CHF 70–110 per person.
meals.dinner: Intimate dinner at a local Poschiavo restaurant — try Albergo Ristorante Croce Federale for traditional Graubünden specialties including Capuns (chard-wrapped dumplings) and Bündner Nusstorte (walnut tart). Pair with a local Graubünden Pinot Noir. Budget CHF 60–90 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Glacier 3000 is located near Les Diablerets in the Vaud Alps — plan the route carefully from Poschiavo (via Chur and Bern or via St. Moritz and Bern). A private driver for the day is strongly recommended given the distance and mountain road conditions. Book cable car tickets online in advance at glacier3000.ch to avoid queues. Weather at 3,000m can change rapidly — bring full winter gear, goggles, and sun protection (UV exposure is intense at altitude).

day_by_day.morning: Embark on the Jungfrau Region Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking experience — a guided full-day excursion to the Jungfrau region (approximately 2.5–3 hours from Poschiavo via train or private transfer). Meet your expert alpine guide in Grindelwald or Wengen and set off on pristine snowshoe trails through UNESCO World Heritage landscapes. The guided route winds through snow-laden forests, across frozen meadows, and offers spectacular views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the snowshoe journey to higher elevations, with the guide sharing insights into alpine ecology, glaciology, and local mountain culture. Optional: ascend to Jungfraujoch — the 'Top of Europe' at 3,454m — via the famous cogwheel railway for an extraordinary high-altitude experience above the clouds. The Aletsch Glacier, Europe's largest glacier, stretches magnificently before you.
day_by_day.evening: Descend to Grindelwald or Interlaken for a celebratory dinner before returning to Poschiavo. The Jungfrau region offers excellent fine dining options in a classic Swiss alpine setting.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at B&B before departure — pack energy-rich snacks for the snowshoe trail.
meals.lunch: Mountain lunch at Bergrestaurant Grindelwald First or a guided picnic on the snowshoe trail — your guide can arrange a gourmet packed lunch with local cheeses, cured meats, dark chocolate, and thermos of hot soup. Budget CHF 40–60 per person.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Schmitte in Grindelwald or The Loft at Beausite Park Hotel Wengen — exceptional alpine cuisine featuring Bernese specialties such as Berner Platte and lake fish, with curated Swiss wine lists. Budget CHF 100–160 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the guided snowshoeing experience in advance through Jungfrau Region's official activity portal or a luxury concierge service. Snowshoes and poles are typically provided by the guide. Wear moisture-wicking base layers, insulated mid-layers, and a waterproof outer shell. The Jungfraujoch railway ticket (CHF 145–200 per person) should be booked well in advance, especially on weekends. The return journey to Poschiavo will be long — consider a private transfer to make it comfortable.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps — wake up for one last panoramic breakfast at B&B Berninahaus Poschiavo Panorama, savoring the mountain views over fresh coffee and a full Swiss spread. Take a leisurely final walk through Poschiavo village, visit the local Sunday market if available, and pick up artisan souvenirs — local cheeses, Bündner Fleisch (air-dried beef), Graubünden wines, and Swiss chocolates.
day_by_day.afternoon: Attend the Swiss Alpine Cheese & Fondue Cultural Evening experience — scheduled as an afternoon/early evening farewell event. Join a traditional Swiss fondue and raclette dinner in a historic mountain chalet in the Verbier or Graubünden region. Learn the art of Swiss cheese-making, the history of fondue culture, and enjoy a convivial, authentic Swiss mountain dining experience with local wines and schnapps. This is the perfect cultural send-off to a magnificent alpine journey.
day_by_day.evening: Final packing and check-out preparations. Arrange a private luxury transfer for your onward journey — whether returning to Zurich Airport, Milan Malpensa, or another destination. Reflect on an extraordinary week in the Swiss Alps over a farewell nightcap of local Graubünden Grappa or Swiss single malt whisky.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — request a special spread with local specialties including Poschiavo's famous Birnbrot (pear bread) and regional honey.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Poschiavo café or village bakery — try a Maluns (potato and flour dish) or a hearty Graubünden soup to keep energy up for travel.
meals.dinner: The Swiss Alpine Cheese & Fondue Cultural Evening serves as the farewell dinner — an immersive multi-course fondue and raclette feast with curated Swiss wine pairings in a historic chalet setting. Budget CHF 120–180 per person including wines.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm the Swiss Alpine Cheese & Fondue experience timing and location in advance — if it is based in Verbier, factor in travel time from Poschiavo (approximately 2.5–3 hours). Alternatively, arrange a private fondue experience closer to Poschiavo through a local catering service or the hotel. Pack all souvenirs and gifts carefully — Swiss cheeses and cured meats may have customs restrictions depending on your destination country. Tip your guides, drivers, and hotel staff generously — 10–15% is customary in Switzerland's luxury hospitality sector. Ensure your private transfer is booked for the correct departure time to reach your airport with ample buffer.
